records.source: וַתֵּ֣רֶא רָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽלְדָה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַתְּקַנֵּ֥א רָחֵ֖ל בַּאֲחֹתָ֑הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ הָֽבָה־לִּ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְאִם־אַ֖יִן מֵתָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי׃
records.gloss: And saw Rachel that not she had borne to Jacob, and was jealous Rachel of her sister; and she said to Jacob, give to me children, and if not, dying [am] I.
pieces: Rachel was bearing Jacob no children, and seeing this she grew jealous of her sister. "Give me sons," she said to Jacob, "or I will die!"

L.1: And Rachel saw that she had borne Jacob no children, and Rachel was jealous of her sister. And she said to Jacob, "Give me children, or else I am dead!"

R.1: Rachel saw that she was not having any children for Jacob, and she became jealous of her sister Leah. She said to Jacob, "Give me children! If you do not, I will die!"

decisions.choice: children: literally "sons"
decisions.reason: The word (banim) is the plural of "son" and covers children in general, but in this chapter the hope is above all for sons, who carried on the family name.

decisions.choice: I am dead: I might as well be dead
decisions.reason: Rachel speaks of herself as already dying. Childlessness was felt as a living death and a public shame (verse 23). The words are bitterly ironic: Rachel does die in childbirth (35:16-19).

decisions.choice: her sister Leah
decisions.reason: Readable names the sister, since the last verses of chapter 29 were about Leah's sons.

records.source: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּרָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲתַ֤חַת אֱלֹהִים֙ אָנֹ֔כִי אֲשֶׁר־מָנַ֥ע מִמֵּ֖ךְ פְּרִי־בָֽטֶן׃
records.gloss: And burned [the] anger of Jacob against Rachel, and he said, in [the] place of God [am] I, who has withheld from you fruit of [the] womb?
pieces: Jacob grew angry with Rachel. "Can I take the place of God?" he said. "It is God who has kept you from having children."

L.2: And Jacob's anger burned against Rachel, and he said, "Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?"

R.2: Jacob became angry with Rachel. He said, "I am not God! God is the one who has kept you from having children."

decisions.choice: Am I in the place of God?: only God gives children
decisions.reason: Jacob's question means that life in the womb is God's gift, not a husband's (29:31; 1 Samuel 1:5). Joseph uses the same words to his brothers in 50:19.

decisions.choice: the fruit of the womb: children
decisions.reason: A common Hebrew picture for offspring (Deuteronomy 7:13; Psalm 127:3).

decisions.choice: having children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה אֲמָתִ֥י בִלְהָ֖ה בֹּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְתֵלֵד֙ עַל־בִּרְכַּ֔י וְאִבָּנֶ֥ה גַם־אָנֹכִ֖י מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And she said, here [is] my slave woman Bilhah; go in to her, that she may bear on my knees, and I may be built up, I also, from her.
pieces: "Take my servant Bilhah," she said. "Lie with her, so that she can give birth on my knees and I may gain a family through her as well."

L.3: And she said, "Here is my slave woman Bilhah; go in to her, so that she may bear on my knees, and I too may be built up through her."

R.3: Then Rachel said, "Here is my servant Bilhah. Sleep with her. She can have a child for me, and I will hold the baby on my knees as my own. Then I can have a family through her."

decisions.choice: bear on my knees: the child counts as Rachel's
decisions.reason: Placing a newborn on one's knees was a sign of taking it as one's own (50:23; compare 48:12). A child born to the slave would be counted as her mistress's, as Sarai had planned with Hagar (16:2).

decisions.choice: be built up: have a family
decisions.reason: As in 16:2, the verb "be built" (banah) sounds like the word for son (ben): a house is built with children.

decisions.choice: slave woman: a female slave
decisions.reason: The word (amah) here, like shifchah in verse 4 and 29:29, describes a woman owned by her mistress. Bilhah was Laban's gift to Rachel (29:29).

decisions.choice: I will hold the baby on my knees as my own
decisions.reason: Readable explains what bearing "on my knees" meant (m1).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m3) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתִּתֶּן־ל֛וֹ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֥ה שִׁפְחָתָ֖הּ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And she gave to him Bilhah her slave woman for a wife, and went in to her Jacob.
pieces: So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and Jacob lay with her.

L.4: So she gave him Bilhah her slave woman as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.

R.4: So Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife, and Jacob slept with her.

decisions.choice: as a wife: a secondary wife
decisions.reason: Bilhah becomes a wife of lower rank and remains Rachel's slave, as Hagar did (16:3). Later she is called a concubine (35:22).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתַּ֣הַר בִּלְהָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And conceived Bilhah and bore to Jacob a son.
pieces: Bilhah became pregnant and bore Jacob a son.

L.5: And Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.

R.5: Bilhah became pregnant and had a son for Jacob.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ דָּנַ֣נִּי אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְגַם֙ שָׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֔י וַיִּתֶּן־לִ֖י בֵּ֑ן עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ דָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And said Rachel, has judged me God, and also has listened to my voice and has given to me a son; therefore she called his name Dan.
pieces: Rachel said, "God has judged my case and heard my cry, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given me a son." That is why she named him Dan.

L.6: And Rachel said, "God has judged me, and has also heard my voice and given me a son." Therefore she called his name Dan.

R.6: Rachel said, "God has judged in my favor. He has heard my prayer and given me a son." So she named him Dan, which means "he judged."

decisions.choice: Dan: "he judged", a pun on dananni, "he has judged me"
decisions.reason: The name Dan comes from the verb din, "to judge", which can mean to give a ruling in someone's favor, to vindicate. Rachel feels that God has taken up her cause against her sister's advantage. Each of the children's names in 29:31-30:24 is explained by a word that sounds like it.

decisions.choice: has judged my case (B); has judged in my favor (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the root of the name; Balanced and Readable show that God took up Rachel's cause, while keeping the word "judge" so the pun can be seen.

decisions.choice: which means "he judged"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, as it does for each child in these chapters (m1).

records.source: וַתַּ֣הַר ע֔וֹד וַתֵּ֕לֶד בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֑ל בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And conceived again and bore Bilhah, slave woman of Rachel, a son second to Jacob.
pieces: Rachel's servant Bilhah became pregnant again and bore Jacob a second son.

L.7: And Bilhah, Rachel's slave woman, conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

R.7: Bilhah became pregnant again and had a second son for Jacob.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל נַפְתּוּלֵ֨י אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀נִפְתַּ֛לְתִּי עִם־אֲחֹתִ֖י גַּם־יָכֹ֑לְתִּי וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ נַפְתָּלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Rachel, wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, also I have prevailed; and she called his name Naphtali.
pieces: Then Rachel said, "I have fought a mighty struggle with my sister, and I have won." So she named him Naphtali.

L.8: And Rachel said, "With wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed." And she called his name Naphtali.

R.8: Rachel said, "My sister and I have fought hard, and I have come out ahead!" So she named him Naphtali, which means "my struggle."

decisions.choice: Naphtali: "my wrestling", a pun on niftalti, "I have wrestled"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the verb Rachel uses (patal, "twist", here "wrestle" or "struggle"). The rivalry between the sisters is pictured as a bout. Jacob himself will wrestle and "prevail" in 32:25-29, where the same verb "prevail" (yakhol) is used.

decisions.choice: wrestlings of God: mighty wrestlings
decisions.reason: Adding "of God" can work as a superlative in Hebrew, "tremendous struggles" (compare 23:6, "a prince of God", a mighty prince). It may also mean a struggle about God's blessing of children. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: a mighty struggle (B); fought hard (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take "of God" as a superlative (m2).

decisions.choice: which means "my struggle"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

records.source: וַתֵּ֣רֶא לֵאָ֔ה כִּ֥י עָמְדָ֖ה מִלֶּ֑דֶת וַתִּקַּח֙ אֶת־זִלְפָּ֣ה שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And saw Leah that she had stopped from bearing, and she took Zilpah her slave woman and gave her to Jacob for a wife.
pieces: Leah, seeing that her childbearing had come to an end, gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.

L.9: And Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, and she took Zilpah her slave woman and gave her to Jacob as a wife.

R.9: Leah was no longer having children. So she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as another wife.

decisions.choice: Leah gives Zilpah: the contest continues
decisions.reason: Leah already had four sons (29:35), but she answers Rachel's plan with the same custom. Zilpah was Laban's gift to Leah (29:24).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה לְיַעֲקֹ֥ב בֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And bore Zilpah, slave woman of Leah, to Jacob a son.
pieces: Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.

L.10: And Zilpah, Leah's slave woman, bore Jacob a son.

R.10: Zilpah had a son for Jacob.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לֵאָ֖ה בָּ֣א גָ֑ד וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ גָּֽד׃
records.gloss: And said Leah, fortune has come; and she called his name Gad.
pieces: "Fortune has come to me!" Leah said, and she named him Gad.

L.11: And Leah said, "Good fortune has come!" And she called his name Gad.

R.11: Leah said, "I am so lucky!" So she named him Gad, which means "good fortune."

decisions.choice: Good fortune has come!: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The letters written in the text form one word, begad, "with fortune" or "how fortunate!". The Masoretes' marginal reading divides it into two words, ba gad, "fortune has come". The meaning is nearly the same, and this translation follows the marginal reading.

decisions.choice: Gad: "good fortune"
decisions.reason: The common noun gad means luck or good fortune; Isaiah 65:11 mentions Gad as the name of a god of fortune. Leah simply rejoices in her luck. Jacob's blessing in 49:19 plays on the name in another way, with gedud, "raiding band".

decisions.choice: which means "good fortune"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m2).

records.source: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת לֵאָ֔ה בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And bore Zilpah, slave woman of Leah, a son second to Jacob.
pieces: Then Zilpah, Leah's servant, bore Jacob a second son.

L.12: And Zilpah, Leah's slave woman, bore Jacob a second son.

R.12: Zilpah had a second son for Jacob.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֔ה בְּאָשְׁרִ֕י כִּ֥י אִשְּׁר֖וּנִי בָּנ֑וֹת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אָשֵֽׁר׃
records.gloss: And said Leah, in my happiness, for call me happy daughters; and she called his name Asher.
pieces: Leah said, "Happy am I! Women everywhere will speak of my happiness." So she named him Asher.

L.13: And Leah said, "In my happiness! For daughters will call me happy." And she called his name Asher.

R.13: Leah said, "I am so happy! Now the other women will say how happy I am." So she named him Asher, which means "happy."

decisions.choice: Asher: "happy", a pun on be'oshri, "in my happiness", and ishsheruni, "they call me happy"
decisions.reason: The name and both of Leah's words come from the root ashar, "happy" or "fortunate", the word that begins Psalm 1 ("Happy is the one ..."). Leah's joy is in the honor other women will give her.

decisions.choice: daughters: women
decisions.reason: "Daughters" here means women in general, as in Song of Songs 6:9.

decisions.choice: Women (B); the other women (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "daughters" (m2).

decisions.choice: which means "happy"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֜ן בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּמְצָ֤א דֽוּדָאִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתָ֔ם אֶל־לֵאָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ אֶל־לֵאָ֔ה תְּנִי־נָ֣א לִ֔י מִדּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And went Reuben in [the] days of [the] harvest of wheat and found mandrakes in the field, and he brought them to Leah his mother; and said Rachel to Leah, give please to me some of [the] mandrakes of your son.
pieces: At wheat harvest time Reuben was out in the fields and came upon some mandrakes, which he brought home to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah, "Please let me have some of the mandrakes your son found."

L.14: And Reuben went in the days of the wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the field and brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."

R.14: When the wheat was being harvested, Reuben found some mandrake plants in a field. He took them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please share your son's mandrakes with me."

decisions.choice: mandrakes: a plant thought to help a woman conceive
decisions.reason: The mandrake has a forked root and fragrant yellow fruit that ripens at wheat harvest, in late spring. In the ancient world it was believed to arouse love and to help childless women conceive. Its name (duda'im) sounds like dodim, "love" (Song of Songs 7:13). Rachel wants it as a fertility charm; in the end it is God who opens her womb (verse 22).

decisions.choice: Reuben: still a boy
decisions.reason: Reuben was Leah's oldest son, and only a few years old at this point. It is natural that a child picking in the fields would bring his find to his mother.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הַמְעַט֙ קַחְתֵּ֣ךְ אֶת־אִישִׁ֔י וְלָקַ֕חַת גַּ֥ם אֶת־דּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל לָכֵן֙ יִשְׁכַּ֤ב עִמָּךְ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה תַּ֖חַת דּוּדָאֵ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And she said to her, [is it] a small thing your taking my husband, and [you would] take also [the] mandrakes of my son? And said Rachel, therefore he will lie with you tonight in exchange for [the] mandrakes of your son.
pieces: But Leah answered, "Is it a small thing to you that you have taken my husband? And now you would take my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said, "Then Jacob may sleep with you tonight; that is the price of your son's mandrakes."

L.15: But she said to her, "Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband? Would you take my son's mandrakes too?" And Rachel said, "Then he shall lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."

R.15: But Leah said, "You have already taken my husband away from me. Now you want to take my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said, "All right. If you give me your son's mandrakes, Jacob can sleep with you tonight."

decisions.choice: you have taken my husband: Jacob lived with Rachel
decisions.reason: Jacob loved Rachel more (29:30), and it seems he spent his nights in her tent. Leah, though the first wife, feels her husband has been taken from her. Rachel has the power to decide whose tent Jacob sleeps in that night.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob, so it is clear who "he" is.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֣ב מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה֮ בָּעֶרֶב֒ וַתֵּצֵ֨א לֵאָ֜ה לִקְרָאת֗וֹ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵלַ֣י תָּב֔וֹא כִּ֚י שָׂכֹ֣ר שְׂכַרְתִּ֔יךָ בְּדוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And came Jacob from the field in the evening, and went out Leah to meet him and said, to me you will come in, for surely I have hired you with [the] mandrakes of my son; and he lay with her that night.
pieces: That evening, as Jacob was coming in from the fields, Leah went out to him and said, "Tonight you are coming to me. I have paid for you with my son's mandrakes." And he spent that night with her.

L.16: And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, "You must come in to me, for I have surely hired you with my son's mandrakes." So he lay with her that night.

R.16: In the evening Jacob came back from the fields. Leah met him on the way and said, "You will sleep in my tent tonight. I paid for you with my son's mandrakes." So that night Jacob slept with her.

decisions.choice: I have surely hired you: Leah paid for the night
decisions.reason: The verb (sakhar) is used of hiring a worker for wages, and it is repeated for emphasis ("hire, I have hired"). It prepares the name Issachar in verse 18. Jacob, who worked for wages for his wives (29:15), is now himself hired.

decisions.choice: paid for you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "paid for", which carries the sense of hiring in natural English; Literal keeps "hired" so the link with Issachar can be seen.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־לֵאָ֑ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּ֥ן חֲמִישִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: And listened God to Leah, and she conceived and bore to Jacob a son fifth.
pieces: God heard Leah's prayer. She conceived and gave Jacob a fifth son.

L.17: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.

R.17: God answered Leah's prayers. She became pregnant and had a fifth son for Jacob.

decisions.choice: God listened to Leah: the child is God's answer
decisions.reason: The text does not credit the mandrakes. It says God listened, which implies Leah had prayed. Rachel had the mandrakes, but Leah had the child.

decisions.choice: heard Leah's prayer (B); answered Leah's prayers (R)
decisions.reason: "Listened to" someone, said of God, means he heard and answered a request; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהִים֙ שְׂכָרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי שִׁפְחָתִ֖י לְאִישִׁ֑י וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשָּׂשכָֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Leah, has given God my wage, because I gave my slave woman to my husband; and she called his name Issachar.
pieces: Leah said, "God has given me my wages for giving my servant to my husband." So she named him Issachar.

L.18: And Leah said, "God has given me my wages, because I gave my slave woman to my husband." So she called his name Issachar.

R.18: Leah said, "God has paid me back because I gave my servant to my husband." So she named him Issachar, which means "reward."

decisions.choice: Issachar: "there is a reward" or "man of wages", a pun on sakhar, "wage"
decisions.reason: The name contains sakhar, "wage" or "hire". It echoes Leah's words to Jacob, "I have hired you" (verse 16), and here her own reason: God has paid her a wage for giving Zilpah to Jacob. Both puns stand together in the name.

decisions.choice: paid me back (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain verb for paying, keeping the idea of a wage.

decisions.choice: which means "reward"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתַּ֤הַר עוֹד֙ לֵאָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּן־שִׁשִּׁ֖י לְּיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And conceived again Leah and bore a son sixth to Jacob.
pieces: Once more Leah became pregnant, and she bore Jacob a sixth son.

L.19: And Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son.

R.19: Leah became pregnant again and had a sixth son for Jacob.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה זְבָדַ֨נִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀אֹתִי֮ זֵ֣בֶד טוֹב֒ הַפַּ֨עַם֙ יִזְבְּלֵ֣נִי אִישִׁ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ זְבֻלֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And said Leah, has endowed me God [with] an endowment good; this time will honor me my husband, for I have borne to him six sons; and she called his name Zebulun.
pieces: Leah said, "God has endowed me with a rich gift. Now at last my husband will honor me, since I have borne him six sons." So she named him Zebulun.

L.20: And Leah said, "God has endowed me with a good endowment; now my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons." So she called his name Zebulun.

R.20: Leah said, "God has given me a wonderful gift. Now my husband will respect me, because I have had six sons for him." So she named him Zebulun, which means "honor."

decisions.choice: Zebulun: a double pun, on zebed, "gift", and yizbeleni, "he will honor me"
decisions.reason: Leah's first words, "God has endowed me with an endowment" (zebadani ... zebed), sound like the name. Her second, yizbeleni, sounds like it even more closely.

decisions.choice: he will honor me: or "he will live with me"
decisions.reason: The verb (zabal) is rare. A related noun means a lofty dwelling (1 Kings 8:13), and the verb may mean to honor, or to live with someone as a husband. Either way Leah hopes at last for Jacob's regard (29:32, 34).

decisions.choice: which means "honor"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name by Leah's second pun (m1, m2).

records.source: וְאַחַ֖ר יָ֣לְדָה בַּ֑ת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמָ֖הּ דִּינָֽה׃
records.gloss: And afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah.
pieces: Afterward she had a daughter, whom she named Dinah.

L.21: And afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah.

R.21: Later Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.

decisions.choice: Dinah: "judgment" or "vindicated", with no reason given
decisions.reason: Unlike her brothers' names, Dinah's is not explained. It comes from the same root as Dan (din, "judge", verse 6). She is mentioned because of what happens to her in chapter 34. Jacob had other daughters too (37:35; 46:7).

records.source: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־רָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־רַחְמָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And remembered God Rachel, and listened to her God, and opened her womb.
pieces: Then God remembered Rachel. He heard her prayers and opened her womb.

L.22: Then God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb.

R.22: Then God remembered Rachel. He answered her prayers and made it possible for her to have children.

decisions.choice: God remembered: God acted on Rachel's behalf
decisions.reason: When God "remembers" someone, he does not recall what he had forgotten; he turns to act for them, as he remembered Noah (8:1) and Abraham (19:29), and later Hannah (1 Samuel 1:19).

decisions.choice: opened her womb: what God did for Leah
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Leah in 29:31, where Rachel was barren. Rachel's child comes from God, not from the mandrakes she bargained for (verse 14).

decisions.choice: made it possible for her to have children
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

records.source: וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אָסַ֥ף אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־חֶרְפָּתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And she conceived and bore a son and said, has taken away God my reproach.
pieces: She conceived and bore a son, and she said, "God has removed my shame."

L.23: And she conceived and bore a son and said, "God has taken away my reproach."

R.23: Rachel became pregnant and had a son. "God has taken my shame away," she said.

decisions.choice: God has taken away (asaf) my reproach: the first pun on Joseph
decisions.reason: Rachel's first saying plays on the name Joseph with the verb asaf, "gather in" or "take away". Her second (verse 24) uses yasaf, "add". Childlessness was a public disgrace for a wife (1 Samuel 1:6; Luke 1:25).

records.source: וַתִּקְרָ֧א אֶת־שְׁמ֛וֹ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר יֹסֵ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י בֵּ֥ן אַחֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And she called his name Joseph, saying, may add YHWH to me a son another.
pieces: She called him Joseph, for she said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} add one more son to me."

L.24: And she called his name Joseph, saying, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} add to me another son!"

R.24: She named him Joseph, which means "may he add," because she said, "I pray {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give me one more son."

decisions.choice: Joseph: "may he add", a pun on yosef, "may he add"
decisions.reason: The name is a verb form, "may he add" (yasaf). With asaf, "he has taken away" (verse 23), Rachel's two sayings give the name two senses: God has taken away her shame, and she prays he will add another son. The prayer is answered in Benjamin (35:16-18).

decisions.choice: which means "may he add"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָלְדָ֥ה רָחֵ֖ל אֶת־יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־לָבָ֔ן שַׁלְּחֵ֨נִי֙ וְאֵ֣לְכָ֔ה אֶל־מְקוֹמִ֖י וּלְאַרְצִֽי׃
records.gloss: And it was, when had borne Rachel Joseph, and said Jacob to Laban, send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land.
pieces: After Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Let me go now, so that I can return to my own home and country.

L.25: And when Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my land.

R.25: After Rachel had Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Let me leave now. I want to go back to my own home and my own country.

decisions.choice: when Rachel had borne Joseph: the end of Jacob's service
decisions.reason: Jacob's second seven years of service for Rachel are now over (29:27-30; 31:41). With a son from the wife he loved, he is ready to go home.

records.source: תְּנָ֞ה אֶת־נָשַׁ֣י וְאֶת־יְלָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֧דְתִּי אֹֽתְךָ֛ בָּהֵ֖ן וְאֵלֵ֑כָה כִּ֚י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת־עֲבֹדָתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַדְתִּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Give [me] my wives and my children, for whom I have served you for them, and I will go; for you, you know my service with which I have served you.
pieces: Let me take my wives and my children, for whom I served you, and go. You yourself know the work I have done for you."

L.26: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go, for you yourself know the service I have rendered you."

R.26: Give me my wives and children. I worked for you to earn them. Let me go. You know how hard I have worked for you."

decisions.choice: Give me my wives and my children: Laban's claim on them
decisions.reason: Jacob asks for leave as a hired worker who had married into the household. Laban would later claim that the daughters, the grandchildren and the flocks were still his (31:43).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לָבָ֔ן אִם־נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ נִחַ֕שְׁתִּי וַיְבָרֲכֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְלָלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said to him Laban, if please I have found favor in your eyes, I have learned by divination that has blessed me YHWH on account of you.
pieces: But Laban said to him, "If you are well disposed toward me, stay. I have learned by omens that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me because of you."

L.27: And Laban said to him, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, [stay;] I have learned by divination that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me because of you."

R.27: But Laban said to him, "Please do me a favor and stay. I have found out by reading signs that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me because of you."

decisions.choice: I have learned by divination: or "I have grown rich"
alternatives: I have grown rich, and the LORD has blessed me
decisions.reason: The verb (nichesh) normally means to practice divination, reading signs and omens (44:5, 15), which the Law later forbids (Leviticus 19:26). A word in a related language means "to prosper", and some take it so here. The common meaning is followed.

decisions.choice: If now I have found favor in your eyes: a sentence left unfinished
decisions.reason: Laban begins a polite request and breaks off; what he wants ("stay") is understood from the context.

decisions.choice: the LORD has blessed me because of you: the promise at work
decisions.reason: God had promised that through Abraham's family others would be blessed (12:3; 28:14). Even Laban sees it, as Potiphar later does with Joseph (39:5).

decisions.choice: [stay] (L); stay (B, R)
decisions.reason: English supplies the request Laban leaves unspoken (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נָקְבָ֧ה שְׂכָרְךָ֛ עָלַ֖י וְאֶתֵּֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And he said, name your wage to me, and I will give [it].
pieces: He went on, "Tell me what wages you want, and I will give them."

L.28: And he said, "Name your wages to me, and I will give it."

R.28: He said, "Tell me what you want me to pay you, and I will pay it."

decisions.choice: Name your wages: Laban's offer of 29:15
decisions.reason: Laban made the same offer twenty years before, and it ended with Jacob working fourteen years for his wives. Jacob has learned to be careful (31:7).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲבַדְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה מִקְנְךָ֖ אִתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, you, you know how I have served you, and how has been your livestock with me.
pieces: Jacob replied, "You know what my service has been to you, and what has become of your herds while I tended them.

L.29: And he said to him, "You yourself know how I have served you, and how your livestock has fared with me.

R.29: Jacob answered, "You know how hard I have worked for you. You know how well your animals have done while I took care of them.

records.source: כִּ֡י מְעַט֩ אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֨ה לְךָ֤ לְפָנַי֙ וַיִּפְרֹ֣ץ לָרֹ֔ב וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ לְרַגְלִ֑י וְעַתָּ֗ה מָתַ֛י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה גַם־אָנֹכִ֖י לְבֵיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: For little [it was] which belonged to you before me, and it has broken out into abundance, and has blessed YHWH you at my foot; and now, when will I do, I also, for my household?
pieces: Before I came you had only a little, and it has multiplied many times over; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you with every step I took. But when am I to provide for my own family?"

L.30: For you had little before I came, and it has increased abundantly, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you at my every step. But now, when shall I provide for my own household also?"

R.30: When I came, you did not have many animals. Now you have a great many. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you wherever I went. But when will I be able to take care of my own family?"

decisions.choice: it has increased: literally "it has broken out"
decisions.reason: The verb (parats) pictures growth bursting through its limits, as in the promise of 28:14, "you will spread out". The same word is used of Jacob in verse 43.

decisions.choice: at my every step: literally "at my foot"
decisions.reason: "At my foot" means wherever I went, at every step. Jacob echoes Laban's words in verse 27: the blessing came with him.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מָ֣ה אֶתֶּן־לָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ לֹא־תִתֶּן־לִ֣י מְא֔וּמָה אִם־תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אָשׁ֛וּבָה אֶרְעֶ֥ה צֹֽאנְךָ֖ אֶשְׁמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And he said, what will I give to you? And said Jacob, not you will give to me anything; if you will do for me this thing, I will again pasture your flock [and] keep [it].
pieces: Laban asked, "What am I to give you?" "Nothing at all," Jacob answered. "Just agree to one condition, and I will once again shepherd your flocks and guard them.

L.31: And he said, "What shall I give you?" And Jacob said, "You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again pasture your flock and keep it:

R.31: Laban asked, "What should I pay you?" Jacob answered, "You do not need to pay me anything. Just agree to this one plan. Then I will keep on taking care of your sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: You shall not give me anything: no wages from Laban's hand
decisions.reason: Jacob asks for nothing Laban already owns. His pay will be whatever odd-colored young are born in the future, so Laban cannot cheat him again by changing what he gives (31:7).

decisions.choice: flock: sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (tson) covers small livestock, both sheep and goats, as the next verses show.

records.source: אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר בְּכָל־צֹֽאנְךָ֜ הַיּ֗וֹם הָסֵ֨ר מִשָּׁ֜ם כָּל־שֶׂ֣ה׀נָקֹ֣ד וְטָל֗וּא וְכָל־שֶׂה־חוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים וְטָל֥וּא וְנָקֹ֖ד בָּעִזִּ֑ים וְהָיָ֖ה שְׂכָרִֽי׃
records.gloss: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there every lamb speckled and spotted, and every lamb dark among the sheep, and spotted and speckled among the goats; and it will be my wage.
pieces: Today I will pass through all your flocks and set apart every animal that is speckled or spotted: the dark ones among the lambs and the spotted and speckled among the goats. These will be my pay.

L.32: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from it every speckled and spotted animal, and every dark one among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and such shall be my wages.

R.32: Today I will go through all your flocks. I will take out every sheep that is dark, and every goat that has spots or speckles. Animals like that will be my pay.

decisions.choice: speckled, spotted and dark: the rare colors
decisions.reason: In that region sheep were normally white and goats black or dark brown. Dark sheep and spotted or speckled goats were few, so Jacob seems to ask for very little.

decisions.choice: animal: one head of the flock (seh)
decisions.reason: The word seh means a single sheep or goat.

decisions.choice: removing from it: who removes them?
alternatives: remove from it (Laban is to remove them)
decisions.reason: The verb form does not show who removes the animals. Laban does it himself in verse 35, so Jacob may be telling him to set them apart. Either way, only animals born afterward are Jacob's.

decisions.choice: every sheep that is dark, and every goat that has spots or speckles
decisions.reason: Readable puts the colors with the animals they apply to, following verses 33 and 35.

records.source: וְעָֽנְתָה־בִּ֤י צִדְקָתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר כִּֽי־תָב֥וֹא עַל־שְׂכָרִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־אֵינֶנּוּ֩ נָקֹ֨ד וְטָל֜וּא בָּֽעִזִּ֗ים וְחוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים גָּנ֥וּב ה֖וּא אִתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And will answer for me my righteousness on a day to come, when you come about my wage before you: all which not speckled and spotted among the goats and dark among the sheep, stolen it [is] with me.
pieces: Later on, my honesty will be my witness. Whenever you come to look over my wages, if I have any goat without speckles or spots, or any lamb that is not dark, you may count it as stolen."

L.33: And my righteousness will answer for me on a day to come, when you come about my wages before you: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats and dark among the lambs, it [shall count as] stolen with me."

R.33: In the future you will see that I am honest. When you come to check the animals you gave me as pay, look at them. If you find any goat that is not spotted or speckled, or any sheep that is not dark, you will know I stole it."

decisions.choice: my honesty: literally "my righteousness"
decisions.reason: The word (tsedaqah) here means fairness in dealings, being in the right. The animals' colors will "testify" that Jacob has kept the bargain.

decisions.choice: honesty (B); I am honest (R)
decisions.reason: In a business dealing the word means honest conduct; Balanced and Readable say so, and Literal keeps "righteousness" (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן הֵ֑ן ל֖וּ יְהִ֥י כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Laban, behold, let it be according to your word.
pieces: Laban said, "Very well, let it be just as you say."

L.34: And Laban said, "Good! Let it be as you have said."

R.34: Laban said, "All right. We will do as you say."

decisions.choice: Good!: literally "look, if only"
decisions.reason: Laban's two words of agreement (hen lu) mean "yes, so be it"; he is quick to accept a bargain that seems to cost him so little.

records.source: וַיָּ֣סַר בַּיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֶת־הַתְּיָשִׁ֜ים הָֽעֲקֻדִּ֣ים וְהַטְּלֻאִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הָֽעִזִּים֙ הַנְּקֻדּ֣וֹת וְהַטְּלֻאֹ֔ת כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־לָבָן֙ בּ֔וֹ וְכָל־ח֖וּם בַּכְּשָׂבִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן בְּיַד־בָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he removed on that day the male goats striped and spotted and all the female goats speckled and spotted, every one that [had] white on it, and every dark one among the sheep, and he gave [them] into [the] hand of his sons.
pieces: But on that very day Laban picked out the male goats with stripes or spots, the female goats with speckles or spots, any with white on them, and every dark lamb, and handed them over to his sons.

L.35: But that same day he removed the striped and spotted male goats and all the speckled and spotted female goats, every one with white on it, and every dark one among the lambs, and put them in the charge of his sons.

R.35: But that same day Laban took away all the male goats that had stripes or spots. He took all the female goats that had speckles or spots, or any white on them. He also took all the dark sheep. He told his sons to take care of them.

decisions.choice: he removed: Laban takes the colored animals for himself
decisions.reason: "He" is Laban. He gives the colored animals to his own sons and sends them far away (verse 36), so that Jacob is left with only white sheep and dark goats, from which few colored young would be expected.

decisions.choice: white (lavan): a pun on Laban
decisions.reason: The word for white is the same as Laban's name. The story plays on it in verse 37 too: Laban the "white" is outwitted by white-peeled sticks.

decisions.choice: But (B, R); Laban (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the contrast with Laban's agreement, and Readable names him.

records.source: וַיָּ֗שֶׂם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים בֵּינ֖וֹ וּבֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן הַנּוֹתָרֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And he put [a] journey of three days between himself and Jacob; and Jacob [was] pasturing the flock of Laban which remained.
pieces: He then moved them a three days' journey away from Jacob, and Jacob was left to pasture the rest of Laban's flocks.

L.36: And he put a three days' journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob pastured the rest of Laban's flock.

R.36: Laban took these animals three days' journey away from Jacob. Jacob went on taking care of the rest of Laban's flocks.

records.source: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב מַקַּ֥ל לִבְנֶ֛ה לַ֖ח וְל֣וּז וְעֶרְמ֑וֹןוַיְפַצֵּ֤ל בָּהֵן֙ פְּצָל֣וֹת לְבָנ֔וֹת מַחְשֹׂף֙ הַלָּבָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמַּקְלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And took for himself Jacob branch[es] of poplar fresh, and almond, and plane tree, and he peeled on them white strips, laying bare the white which [was] on the branches.
pieces: Jacob then took freshly cut sticks of poplar, almond and plane wood and peeled bark off them in strips, baring the white wood underneath.

L.37: And Jacob took for himself fresh branches of poplar and almond and plane tree, and peeled white stripes in them, laying bare the white that was in the branches.

R.37: Then Jacob cut some fresh branches from poplar, almond and plane trees. He peeled off strips of bark so that the branches had white stripes on them.

decisions.choice: poplar (livneh), white (lavan): more puns on Laban
decisions.reason: The word for poplar, the white stripes and the white wood all sound like Laban's name. Laban, "white", who had taken away every animal with white on it (verse 35), is beaten with white.

decisions.choice: almond and plane tree
decisions.reason: The almond (luz) has the same name as the town Luz, the old name of Bethel (28:19). The plane tree (ermon) is a tall tree with bark that peels in patches.

records.source: וַיַּצֵּ֗ג אֶת־הַמַּקְלוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּצֵּ֔ל בָּרֳהָטִ֖ים בְּשִֽׁקֲת֣וֹת הַמָּ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨אןָ הַצֹּ֤אן לִשְׁתּוֹת֙ לְנֹ֣כַח הַצֹּ֔אן וַיֵּחַ֖מְנָה בְּבֹאָ֥ן לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he set the branches which he had peeled in the troughs, in the watering channels, where came the flock to drink, in front of the flock; and they were in heat when they came to drink.
pieces: He set the peeled sticks in the troughs at the watering places, right in front of the animals as they came to drink, for they came into heat when they came to drink.

L.38: And he set the branches that he had peeled in front of the flock in the troughs, at the watering places where the flock came to drink. And they mated when they came to drink.

R.38: He put the peeled branches in the water troughs where the animals came to drink. The branches were right in front of them. The animals were ready to mate when they came to drink.

decisions.choice: they mated: they came into heat
decisions.reason: The verb (yacham) means to be in heat, warm with desire. When the animals gathered at the water they were ready to breed, and Jacob chose that moment.

records.source: וַיֶּחֱמ֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן אֶל־הַמַּקְל֑וֹת וַתֵּלַ֣דְןָ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּטְלֻאִֽים׃
records.gloss: And were in heat the flock at the branches, and bore the flock striped, speckled, and spotted.
pieces: The flocks bred in front of the sticks, and their young were born striped, speckled and spotted.

L.39: And the flocks mated in front of the branches, and the flocks bore young that were striped, speckled and spotted.

R.39: The animals mated in front of the branches. Then they gave birth to young ones with stripes, speckles and spots.

decisions.choice: the branches and the colored young: what caused it?
decisions.reason: People of that time believed that what a mother saw at the moment of conceiving could mark her young. The narrator reports what Jacob did and what followed, without endorsing the method. Jacob later says that God gave him the flocks and showed him in a dream which males would mate (31:9-12); the true cause was God's blessing, not the sticks.

records.source: וְהַכְּשָׂבִים֮ הִפְרִ֣יד יַעֲקֹב֒ וַ֠יִּתֵּן פְּנֵ֨י הַצֹּ֧אן אֶל־עָקֹ֛ד וְכָל־ח֖וּם בְּצֹ֣אן לָבָ֑ן וַיָּֽשֶׁת־ל֤וֹ עֲדָרִים֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁתָ֖ם עַל־צֹ֥אן לָבָֽן׃
records.gloss: And the lambs separated Jacob, and he set [the] faces of the flock toward [the] striped and every dark one in [the] flock of Laban; and he made for himself flocks by himself, and not he put them with [the] flock of Laban.
pieces: Jacob kept the lambs apart, but turned the animals to face the striped and dark ones in Laban's flock. In this way he built up flocks of his own, which he kept apart from Laban's.

L.40: And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flock toward the striped and all the dark ones in Laban's flock. And he put his own droves apart by themselves and did not put them with Laban's flock.

R.40: Jacob separated the young animals. He made the rest of the flock face the striped and dark animals in Laban's flock. In this way Jacob built up his own flocks and kept them away from Laban's animals.

decisions.choice: the sense of the verse is not clear
alternatives: Jacob separated the lambs, and turned the flock toward Laban's striped and dark animals
decisions.reason: The verse is compressed, and it is not certain which animals were separated or which faced which. The likely sense is that Jacob kept the colored young that were his apart, but let the breeding animals see them, so that more colored young would be born; and he kept his growing flock away from Laban's.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּכָל־יַחֵם֮ הַצֹּ֣אן הַמְקֻשָּׁרוֹת֒ וְשָׂ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֧ב אֶת־הַמַּקְל֛וֹת לְעֵינֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן בָּרֳהָטִ֑ים לְיַחְמֵ֖נָּה בַּמַּקְלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And it was, in every mating of the flock, the strong ones, and put Jacob the branches before the eyes of the flock in the troughs, that they might mate among the branches;
pieces: Each time the sturdier animals were mating, Jacob laid the sticks in the troughs in full view of the flock, so that they bred among the sticks;

L.41: And whenever the stronger of the flock were mating, Jacob would lay the branches in the troughs before the eyes of the flock, so that they would mate among the branches;

R.41: Whenever the strong, healthy animals were ready to mate, Jacob put the branches in the troughs in front of them. That way they mated near the branches.

decisions.choice: the stronger: literally "the bound ones"
alternatives: the ones bred early in the season
decisions.reason: The word (mequsharot) seems to mean firm or sturdy, strong animals. Some take it to mean the animals that bred in the spring, when stronger young were born.

records.source: וּבְהַעֲטִ֥יף הַצֹּ֖אן לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ים וְהָיָ֤ה הָעֲטֻפִים֙ לְלָבָ֔ן וְהַקְּשֻׁרִ֖ים לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: and in the feebleness of the flock, not he put [them]; and were the feeble [ones] to Laban and the strong [ones] to Jacob.
pieces: but when the weaker animals mated, he left the sticks out. In this way the feeble animals ended up as Laban's and the strong ones as Jacob's.

L.42: but when the flock was feeble he did not put them there. So the feebler ones were Laban's and the stronger Jacob's.

R.42: But when the weak animals were ready to mate, he did not put out the branches. So Laban got the weak animals, and Jacob got the strong ones.

records.source: וַיִּפְרֹ֥ץ הָאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי־לוֹ֙ צֹ֣אן רַבּ֔וֹת וּשְׁפָחוֹת֙ וַעֲבָדִ֔ים וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And increased the man very very, and there were to him flocks many and female slaves and male slaves and camels and donkeys.
pieces: So Jacob grew richer and richer. He came to own great flocks, servants both female and male, camels and donkeys.

L.43: And the man grew exceedingly rich and had many flocks, and female and male slaves, and camels and donkeys.

R.43: So Jacob became very, very rich. He had large flocks of sheep and goats, many servants, and camels and donkeys.

decisions.choice: the man grew exceedingly rich: the promise fulfilled
decisions.reason: The verb is the "break out" of verse 30 and of God's promise at Bethel, "you will spread out" (28:14). Jacob now has the kind of wealth Abraham (12:16) and Isaac (26:13-14) had.

decisions.choice: female and male slaves
decisions.reason: The words (shifchah, eved) are the usual words for owned servants, as with Abraham's household (12:16).

decisions.choice: grew exceedingly rich
decisions.reason: The repeated "very" is a Hebrew way to say "extremely"; each level gives it in English form.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".
